P1.evidence: Notes and application were genuinely read back, and the rep opened on the most personal item in them: 'I just want to read. I had some notes on you here from earlier... I wanted to peek back at your application... First of all, man, I'm sorry for the loss of the relationship. That's the first thing I noticed.' The frame was three parts plus next steps — 'where we're at in our fitness journey, where we're trying to get to, and what's kind of missing in the middle... From there, we can talk about some next steps, map out a plan.' Agreement taken with 'Does that all sound good?' and the open question ran: 'what do you feel we could potentially help you with? Give me a rundown.'

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight confirmed. Work asked at the open and the sitting question asked directly — 'with your work, do you do a lot of sitting?' — which produced the box-truck detail. Injuries asked properly and probed: 'Any other, like, injuries or anything else that might inhibit working out at all?' and 'it's not inhibiting work right now at all, is it?' Current training established as nil. Health conditions were never asked directly; the blood pressure medication came out of the catch-all 'is there anything else that you feel I might need to know', and the family history came out of the why-ladder. Diet was never asked at all — the rep pitched the nutrition pillar first and only afterwards did the prospect volunteer 'I always just eat whatever I want. I really don't pay attention to what I eat.' Sleep and energy not asked.

P3.evidence: The why-ladder was the strongest part of the call. 'What is the look that you actually want?' got the six-pack answer, and the rep noticed the repetition and drove on it: 'you brought up longevity like 18 times since we started talking... why is it so important specifically?' That produced the family health history and the mother's death at 57, and the rep followed it with 'Sounds like you might have seen one too many things over the years, huh?' Kids were asked twice and the answer was none. Nothing was asked about mobility versus strength versus energy, nothing about a physical thing he cannot currently do, and the reflect-back was folded into a line-in-the-sand assertion rather than a 'this isn't really about the weight' mirror.

P4.evidence: Best-run P4 in the batch. 'What have you tried so far to kind of get back in shape?' then the regain probed directly: 'it looked like you'd lost a lot of weight and it's come back for you.' Then the standout move — he caught an inconsistency in the timeline and went back for it: 'it happened a month ago, but it's also been three months since the schedules have been more lined up, so there's still kind of two months in between that. What happened during those two months?' That is the phase working as designed. The prospect then named the gap himself: 'That's someone to hold me accountable.' The 'information isn't the problem' challenge was softened into 'why are you feeling like you might need a little bit of help with this, out of curiosity?'

P5.evidence: The two-year question was never asked. What ran instead were alternative-plan questions — 'if we don't pursue the coaching, what's the other option?' and later 'if we don't move forward with this, what's the plan, do you think?' — and both produced the opposite of a consequence frame: the prospect calmly described a viable fallback (Beachbody plus self-taught kettlebells) and said 'The plan for longevity is not change.' That answer made the offer optional rather than necessary and it was never challenged. The line in the sand was asserted by the rep and confirmed rather than asked: 'it really seems like we're ready to draw a line in sand and get this fricking thing figured out. Is that what I'm understanding?'

P6.evidence: The all-in question ran close to script and before the price: 'provided we can figure out like the logistics and the details and stuff like that, like, I want to triple check Damien. Like, are you in a position where it's like, hey dude, I'm all in on this? I'm going to show up for the workouts.' The yes came with a scheduling condition — training has to fit around two jobs — which the rep clarified and resolved on the call. The belief question ('do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner') was never asked, which matters for a prospect whose last attempt succeeded and then reversed.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected, so step 1 is a miss and steps 2-4 were unreachable. No onboarding call, no agreement, no Skool link, and the follow-up was left as 'I'll shoot you a text in a week or something like that.'

objection_plays.detail: The most complete OC in the batch. Isolation ran: 'finances aside, before we dive into that, is there anything else at all that's keeping you from being less than 100% certain that like this is the right thing and now is the right time?' Should-versus-how ran: 'we're not in like a should I do this place... it's just right now it's a matter of how do we make this work on the financial side.' The break-it-up move ran. The permission question ran almost verbatim: 'are you open to having like an open and honest conversation about where we're at financially and either we can find something that does work right now or worst case, we can create a game plan to work towards in the future?' Then five of the six financial-picture items were actually gathered — liquid cash ($2,000), investments ($7,000-8,000), monthly income ($4,000), monthly surplus (about $1,000), and credit access (none, credit 'terrible'). Only the card-by-card available-versus-used breakdown was skipped, and only because there are no cards. Scored on adherence this is a clean run. Scored on judgement it is the worst outcome in the batch: the play returned an unambiguous cannot-afford and the rep responded by extending the plan to six payments totalling $7,200 rather than treating the answer as disqualifying. The script has no instruction to stop, which is a script problem as much as a rep problem.

Trigger was explicit — 'I'm probably gonna have to think about this. Probably need some time to sit down and kind of look at my budget.' The rep ran one improvised move, 'what if we just said, [screw] it and do it?', backed by 'you can't bring it to the grave with you' and a longevity appeal. None of the scripted sequence ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision', no closing 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. He then spent the remaining ten minutes probing what the prospect would cut rather than working the objection.

Trigger arrived clearly at the end: 'it might not be right for me at this moment, you know, financially, but I know it's definitely going to be right for me financially in the future' and 'give me six months and I should be able to do it.' Not one move was run — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', and notably not 'the only thing you can control is right now', which would have connected directly to the prospect's own line about focusing on what he can control. The rep agreed to stay in contact instead.

Script gap — no disqualification branch. OC ends in either 'find a way that works now' or 'create a game plan for the future', with nothing for a prospect whose disclosed numbers make the purchase genuinely unsafe. This prospect said 'if I miscalculate just the slightest, then things can really get real ugly in my life' and 'I don't have any family besides my wife... probably end up on the streets.' The correct commercial and ethical move was to stop selling and offer to revisit, and the playbook gives the rep no permission or language to do that.

Script gap — a free or near-free substitute the prospect has already used successfully. He holds a dormant Beachbody On Demand subscription and named it twice as his fallback: 'I still have my Beachbody On Demand account, so I'm definitely going to get back and start doing that.' This is the same gap logged against the Badrane Hriouch call. The rep did partially differentiate on accountability, and the prospect actually made the argument for him — 'there is no accountability. The only person holding you accountable is yourself' — but nothing in the script converts that into a price justification.

notes: P1 and P4 were textbook and P5 was absent, which is the pattern across this rep's calls — but here the missing consequence frame did specific damage, because the fallback question let the prospect state a credible free alternative and it was never contested. The urgent coaching point is not technique: the financial picture ran correctly, returned a clear no, and the rep escalated the offer anyway. Reps need an explicit stop rule and the authority to use it.
